The compound is identified as a target of several entities, including Multidrug resistance-associated protein 7 and Guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2, which in turn are targets of other molecules. These interactions imply that the compound may exert its effects through diverse molecular mechanisms, potentially involving G-protein signaling or transport-related pathways. The evidence is supported by high scores in the final score, indicating a strong likelihood of a functional relationship. However, the exact mechanism by which the compound interacts with ATR remains unclear, and further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct involvement of the compound in ATR activity.
